name: Jirav
summary: Jirav builds three-statement budgets, rolling forecasts and multiple scenarios, and compares plan with actuals in its reporting. A business pays $10,000 a year for Starter or $15,000 for Pro, and a separate wholesale price list for accounting and CFO advisory firms starts at $50 a month.

facts.text: Jirav publishes two price lists: business pricing in dollars per year, and wholesale pricing for accounting and CFO advisory firms in dollars per month.
The business pricing page shows model duration of 24, 48 and 84 months across Starter, Professional and Enterprise, and 2, 3 and 5 active plans.
The reporting page says users can view performance from one budget to the next or plan versus actuals, with commentary on variance reports.
The business pricing page offers a demo and does not mention a free trial.

plans.name: Starter (business)
plans.notes: Up to 5 planning departments, 2 admin or editor users and 24 months of model duration

plans.name: Pro (business)
plans.notes: Up to 15 planning departments, 5 admin or editor users and 48 months of model duration

plans.name: Enterprise (business)
plans.notes: Contact for a quote; 15 admin or editor users and 84 months of model duration

plans.name: Controller Essentials (accounting firms)
plans.notes: Wholesale price for accounting and CFO advisory firms: 2 plans and a 1-year forecast

plans.name: CFO Enterprise (accounting firms)
plans.notes: Wholesale price for accounting and CFO advisory firms: 5 active scenarios and a 7-year forecast

hiddenCosts: The wholesale list says "starting at" and does not say what the unit is, so confirm what a client is counted as before comparing it with the business price list.
